title.narrative: Ensuring the Safety of Female Journalists, Promoting Freedom of Expression and Guarantees against Impunity in The Gambia

description.narrative: The Gambia Press Union (GPU), the umbrella body for media practitioners in The Gambia, is registered with the Attorney General’s Chambers in April 1979. With both trade union and professional pursuits, the GPU aims to safeguard the welfare of media practitioners while promoting media professionalism through training programmes, freedom of expression and access to information. Membership of the GPU consists of professional journalists and other media workers drawn from across the mix of mass media – radio, television, print and online. The Union has six affiliate local journalists’ organisations (Women Journalists of The Gambia, Young Journalists Association, Network of community radio Journalists, sports journalists of The Gambia, Network of Agricultural Reporters and Network of human rights journalists). GPU is also affiliated with regional and international media organisations such as the International Federation of Journalists (IFJ), Federation of African Journalists (FAJ), International Freedom of Expression Exchange (IFEX) and West African Journalists Association (WAJA). It is also part of other national alliances and coalitions such as the CSO Coalition on Elections, and CSO Coalition on Access to Information. In over four decades of its existence, the GPU has evolved into a prominent national organisation of international repute. With a growing membership, an expanding network of national and international affiliates and partners, the Union has a well-staffed secretariat.
